about.title: Fairfax Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Fairfax is a small town, roughly 7,626 people tucked into the hills of Marin County, and that closeness means a sudden death is felt well beyond one household. Public records for 2025 show 17 injury collisions in town, 19 people hurt, and one life lost on the road. One is a small number until it is your family. Most reported crashes cluster along Sir Francis Drake Boulevard, Bolinas Road, Broadway, and Center Boulevard, with a noticeable bump on Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. A wrongful death claim in California is a civil action, separate from anything the district attorney may or may not pursue. It belongs first to the spouse or domestic partner and children, then to certain dependents and heirs. The filing window is generally two years from the date of death, and shorter when a public agency is involved. LawProactive is not a law firm. We connect Fairfax families with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency, so you can grieve while someone else carries the paperwork.

whyChoose.title: Why Fairfax Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits standing to the spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can sort out where your family stands before anything is filed.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: The general limit is two years from the date of death, but claims involving a government entity move on a much shorter clock. Getting connected quickly protects your ability to act.

items.title: The full scope of loss
items.desc: Recoverable losses include funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. Nothing is owed unless there is a recovery.

items.question: The crash happened on Sir Francis Drake Boulevard and a town or county vehicle was involved. Does that change anything?
items.answer: It can. When a public agency such as the Town of Fairfax or Marin County is a potential defendant, California requires a formal claim on a timeline far shorter than the usual two years. An attorney can tell you whether that shortened window applies and what has to be submitted. Reaching out sooner rather than later keeps that door open.

items.question: My sibling died. Can I bring a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Standing goes first to the surviving spouse or domestic partner and children. Siblings and other relatives may qualify only in specific situations, such as when there is no spouse or child, or when they were financially dependent on the person who died. An attorney can review your family's circumstances and explain who is eligible.

items.question: The other driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and runs on its own track, separate from any criminal prosecution. The criminal case can sometimes provide useful evidence, but your two-year deadline does not pause while it plays out. Your attorney can coordinate the timing so nothing is missed.
